title: Diagnostic challenges in tuberculous meningitis: a case report with negative genexpert result
case_prompt:
A 22-year-old woman from Eastern Nepal presented with a 2-day history of fever (103 °F), agitation, earache, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, and neck pain. She denied pulmonary or systemic TB symptoms. She had no comorbidities.  
On examination: T 103 °F; BP 130/80 mm Hg; HR 96 bpm; RR 22 breaths/min; SpO₂ 99% on room air. She appeared ill and irritable, with neck stiffness and positive Kernig and Brudzinski signs; there was no lymphadenopathy or other focal findings.  
Laboratory studies: Hb 10.2 g/dL; WBC 23,500/mm³ (90% neutrophils, 7% lymphocytes); ESR 58 mm/h; Na 133 mmol/L; Ca 8.0 mg/dL; Mg 1.2 mg/dL; HIV, HBsAg, HCV, and VDRL/RPR nonreactive; dengue serology negative; sputum AFB negative. Noncontrast head CT and chest radiograph were normal.  
She received empiric IV ampicillin, ceftriaxone, vancomycin, and acyclovir. Lumbar puncture yielded clear, light-yellow CSF with cobweb coagulum. CSF analysis showed: total nucleated cell count 195/µL (90% lymphocytes, 10% neutrophils); glucose 23 mg/dL; protein (albumin) 200 mg/dL; ADA 12 IU/L; GeneXpert MTB/RIF negative; serum CRP positive; anti-JE IgM in serum and CSF negative.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Bacterial meningitis was considered given the acute fever, headache, and neck stiffness, but the CSF profile was lymphocytic rather than neutrophilic — “Total cell count in CSF was 195/μl with lymphocyte predominance (90% lymphocytes and 10% neutrophils).”  
2. Viral encephalitis was entertained due to lymphocytic pleocytosis and altered mental status, yet there was no clinical improvement with antiviral therapy — “Despite the empirical treatment, as there was no improvement in the patient’s condition, antitubercular therapy was started on second day of admission…”  
3. Japanese encephalitis was specifically excluded by negative serology — “The serological test for Japanese Encephalitis (anti-JE IgM in serum and CSF) was also negative.”  
4. Tuberculous meningitis was diagnosed based on characteristic CSF biochemistry and elevated ADA despite a negative GeneXpert assay — “The adenosine deaminase (ADA) enzyme level in CSF fluid was high (12 IU/l).”
